why.text: Hot, dry summers ripen the grapes quickly. The Superior subzone lies on albariza, the best soil for generosos and liqueur wines.

styles.text: Young whites, unaged or aged; generosos Fino (unfortified or fortified), Amontillado, Oloroso and Palo Cortado; sweet Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel; Generoso de Licor, Pale Cream and Cream.

climate.text: Semi-continental Mediterranean: long, hot, dry summers and short, relatively mild winters, which speed up ripening.

soil.text: The Superior subzone covers albariza soils.

tastes.text: Young whites: pale yellow to pale gold, fruity and floral, noticeable acidity. Fino: straw to old gold, slightly bitter, saline. Oloroso: old gold to dark mahogany, slightly unctuous, persistent. Pedro Ximénez: old gold to deep mahogany or jet, very dense.

styles.name: Fino
styles.text: Straw yellow to old gold, biological ageing, yeasty, slightly bitter and saline.

styles.name: Amontillado
styles.text: Gold to deep amber; nuts and wood, maybe varnish; acidic and persistent.

styles.name: Oloroso
styles.text: Old gold to dark mahogany; nuts and wood; slightly unctuous and persistent.

styles.name: Pedro Ximénez
styles.text: Sweet liqueur wine, old gold to deep mahogany or jet, raisined, very dense.

why.text: Half the area lies above 1,000 m: grapes ripen slowly, with a daily temperature swing. Most vines grow on poor brown soils over siliceous rock.

styles.text: White, rosado and red wines, plus sparkling wines and sweet wines from overripe grapes.

climate.text: A daily swing between highs and lows; absolute highs average 39 °C and lows -4 °C; 450 mm of rain a year over about 70 rainy days.

soil.text: Mostly brown soils over siliceous metamorphic rock, very poor in organic matter, phosphorus and nitrogen; some brown limy soils with little humus.

altitude.text: Half of the area lies above 1,000 m above sea level.

tastes.text: Reds: red with violet to mahogany tones; frank, pleasant aromas. Whites: greenish yellow to amber; fresh to evolved aromas. Rosés: pale pink to light red; fresh to evolved aromas.

styles.name: Vino de uvas sobremaduradas
styles.text: White, rosé or red wine made from overripe grapes.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad
styles.text: White, rosé or red sparkling wine with persistent foam.

why.text: A flat Guadalquivir lowland near Doñana, where Atlantic influence softens a Mediterranean climate. Generosos age in criaderas and solera or by vintage (añadas).

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, young to aged; generosos, unfortified or fortified; generosos de licor and sweet liqueur wines, including mistelas.

climate.text: Mediterranean with Atlantic touches; flat to gently rolling land in the Guadalquivir depression, next to Doñana National Park.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to old gold; young ones green apple and floral, others stone fruit; noticeable acidity. Reds: cherry to brick red; perceptible fruit; astringency and density. Rosés: pale pink to reddish pink; fruity, floral.

styles.name: Condado Viejo
styles.text: Generoso, old gold to dark mahogany; nuts and wood, maybe varnish.

styles.name: Generoso
styles.text: Dry, aged biologically or oxidatively; straw yellow to dark mahogany, nutty.

styles.name: Mistela
styles.text: Liqueur wine, gold to deep mahogany, fruity aromas, dense on the palate.

styles.name: Gran Reserva
styles.text: Red aged at least 60 months, 18 in oak casks up to 330 l.

why.text: Strong southern sun lets grapes ripen and overripen; mountains, sea and Atlantic air temper the heat. In drier spots growers sun-dry grapes for sweet wines.

styles.text: Dry unfortified wine, yellow to amber with age; dry and sweet liqueur wines; sweet wines from overripe or raisined grapes.

climate.text: Mediterranean with very high sunshine, shaped by mountain relief, the nearby sea and an Atlantic transition.

soil.text: Slate in the Axarquía and Montes, limestone in the Serranía de Ronda, albariza in Manilva, deep brown-limestone soils in the Norte.

tastes.text: Dry wine: yellow to amber, penetrating, powerful aroma. Liqueur wines: intense nose, integrated alcohol; sweet ones unctuous and persistent. Raisined-grape wines: pale yellow to old gold; concentrated, acid-sweet balance.

styles.name: Dulce Natural
styles.text: Sweet liqueur wine showing varietal, fermentation and fortification aromas.

styles.name: Vino de uvas pasificadas
styles.text: Sweet wine from raisined grapes, pale yellow to old gold, very unctuous.

styles.name: Vino Naturalmente Dulce
styles.text: Sweet overripe-grape wine, fresh, lively, unctuous and persistent.

why.text: Europe's southernmost sierras run down to the Mediterranean. Ripening temperatures stay moderate and drop at night despite very strong sun; soils drain well.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, from fresh young wines to oak-aged ones; also clearly sweet reds from overripe grapes.

climate.text: Mediterranean: very high sunshine, moderate ripening temperatures that drop at night, and many mesoclimates shaped by relief and sea.

soil.text: Well-drained soils of medium to low fertility.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to old gold; fruity. Rosés: onion skin to reddish pink with ruby tones; fruity, floral. Reds: violet to brick red; fruity, with astringency. Overripe reds: violet to dark cherry.

why.text: Almost flat farmland lies beside the Guadalquivir marshes, on well-drained albariza. Summers are long and harsh, with highs that can top 40 °C.

styles.text: Young whites; reds from young to gran reserva; flor-aged generosos; liqueur and natural sweet wines; mistela.

climate.text: Warm continental Mediterranean, softened by Atlantic currents; mild autumn and spring; long, harsh summer with highs that can pass 40 °C, August hottest.

soil.text: Almost all land is flat. Deep, well-drained albariza dominates the vineyards.

tastes.text: Reds: bright ruby to deep cherry; ripe fruit, vanilla and coffee when oaked; fleshy, full-bodied, velvety. Whites: very pale, fruity, dry or off-dry. Flor de Lebrija: straw yellow, almond, dry.

styles.name: Flor de Lebrija
styles.text: Dry generoso aged under flor; straw yellow, almond aroma, light on the palate.

styles.name: Lebrija Old Vino Seco
styles.text: Generoso in amber to mahogany, with a walnut aroma.

styles.name: Lebrija Old Dulce
styles.text: Generoso de licor, amber to dark mahogany, full-bodied, pungent, muted aroma.

styles.name: Dulce natural
styles.text: Gold to mahogany; honey, caramel and raisin aromas; velvety, glyceric.

why.text: Vines suited to the climate grow on albariza, a soft marl that holds moisture. Flor yeast and soleras age the wines.

styles.text: Dry generosos (fino, amontillado, oloroso, palo cortado), unfortified or fortified; sweet Pedro Ximénez, Moscatel and Dulce; sweetened generosos de licor.

climate.text: Warm: average winter lows around 5 °C, summer highs around 35 °C; over 300 sunny days and about 600 mm of rain a year, mostly in November, December and March.

soil.text: Albarizas: soft marls that hold moisture well.

tastes.text: From straw-yellow, fluid finos to ebony, unctuous Pedro Ximénez. All balanced, sapid, intense and persistent, with a chalky, sapid note, clearest in the driest, youngest wines.

styles.name: Fino, Amontillado, Oloroso, Palo Cortado
styles.text: Vino Generoso type, dry: at most 4 g/l sugar; long-aged ones up to 9 g/l.

why.text: Sanlúcar cellars stay humid all year, helped by Atlantic night breezes. Ageing under flor gains greatly from that humidity and from the solera system.

styles.text: Generoso wine, straw yellow to amber, aged at least two years under flor in Sanlúcar de Barrameda; sold as vino or, fortified, as vino de licor.

climate.text: Warm, with the sea close by. Cellars in Sanlúcar stay more humid all year and milder in winter and summer than the rest of the zone.

soil.text: Mostly albariza, a soft white marl that holds moisture; also darker, more fertile «barros» in the hollows and sandy «arenas» near the coast.

tastes.text: Straw yellow to amber; at least two of white flowers, nuts or yeast (fresh bread dough); dry and saline, sometimes slightly acid and bitter.

styles.name: Manzanilla
styles.text: Generoso aged wholly under flor, only in Sanlúcar de Barrameda cellars.
